analysis.title: End of Week Market Intelligence: set-up
key_insights: US stocks were trading higher on Friday 10/9 and on pace for about a 1% weekly gain for the S&P 500, with investors positioning ahead of 3Q earnings season and the Sept CPI report due next week.

The week's data was unremarkable: ISM services was unremarkable, U Michigan consumer sentiment kept eroding, and PEP and DAL 3Q26 results point to shifting consumer tastes (services over soda) and rising input costs, especially jet fuel.
The US 10-year Treasury yield is little changed on the week at 5.25%. Brent has risen a touch.
Ben Snider expects most S&P 500 companies to beat consensus estimates in 3Q, with 27% y/y EPS growth for the index. The focus is AI monetization and productivity gains.
Richard Ramsden's big bank 3Q26 preview is titled cautious optimism: focus on a capital markets slowdown, strong NII, and moderating capital returns. Big bank results come next week.
10-year yields are now sustainably above 5%, and signs of sovereign debt stress in Europe are emerging, notably in France (Jari Stehn, ECB note on rising sovereign stress).
GS attributes the rate rise to a post-pandemic inflation impulse from higher import tariffs and the US-Iran War's effect on oil and refined product supply.
The September FOMC minutes showed 'most' participants saw another increase as likely appropriate by year end. The Fed raised rates in September, the first hike this cycle.
GS expects the second Fed hike in December but sees a strong chance the FOMC ultimately concludes further tightening is unnecessary. GS acknowledges it could be wrong that rates recede from here.
Pierfrancesco Mei estimates the drag on US GDP growth could be slightly over 0.5pp if rates stay higher for longer.

Alec Phillips: prediction markets moved further toward Democrats taking the Senate over the past week, helped by polls in Kansas and New Hampshire. Markets imply a more than 90% chance Democrats net the three seats needed for the House, and the generic ballot margin widened another 0.5pp toward Democrats.
Hedge funds are described as cautious on stocks amid rates and energy volatility (Mark Wilson, weekly Markets podcast).

Tim Moe: Taiwan and Korea now make up half of the MXAPJ index weight, displacing China, driven by a handful of AI hardware suppliers. GS flags this concentration as possibly a canary in the coal mine, though it is currently thought of as a new normal.
Next week: big bank earnings, Sept CPI on Wednesday, Philly Fed on Thursday, plus retail sales, industrial production and housing turnover. Hyperscalers report at the end of October.

market_movers.rationale: Bonnie Herzog: slight Q3 beat, FY26 EPS guidance lowered as expected given continued North American pressure. Maintain Buy.

earnings_insights: PEP 3Q26 reported: slight beat versus consensus, FY26 EPS guidance lowered, as expected given North American pressure (Bonnie Herzog, GS).
DAL 3Q26 reported: slightly below consensus, while the 4Q revenue outlook is ahead of consensus (Catie O'Brien, GS). Jet fuel costs are rising.
S&P 500 3Q26 EPS growth forecast at 27% y/y (Ben Snider estimate), with most companies expected to beat consensus.
Big bank 3Q26 results are due next week. GS expects strong NII and a capital markets slowdown, with moderating capital returns (Ramsden preview).
